topic: Loki killed his own father Harald to stop Imu's plan to turn Elbaph into a weapon
title: Loki Killed His Own King To Save Elbaph
description: Elbaph still calls Loki the Accursed Prince. Here's why I think that's backwards, and what chapter 1170 actually shows him stopping. Hero or traitor?
comment: Hero or traitor: does Loki killing his own father make him Elbaph's best defense, or just a kinslayer who got lucky?

lines.text: Loki killed his own king. Elbaph still calls him a traitor.

shot.fallback: giant prince standing over a fallen king

lines.text: But I don't think that's betrayal. I think it's the opposite.

shot.fallback: giant warrior facing a difficult truth

lines.text: Elbaph's king, Harald, was secretly taking orders from Imu himself.

shot.fallback: giant king kneeling before a shadowy ruler

lines.text: Imu wanted every giant in Elbaph turned into a weapon for the World Government.
Harald tried to resist that order. Loki says it never stopped. It just moved.
So Loki made the one choice nobody else in Elbaph was willing to make.

shot.fallback: giant prince facing an impossible decision

lines.text: He killed his own father, before that weapon could ever finish forming.

shot.fallback: giant prince striking down a transformed king

lines.text: That's chapter 1170, the one fans remember for the fruit, not the reason behind it.

shot.fallback: giant prince eating a glowing fruit

lines.text: Years later, his hybrid dragon form is still fighting Imu, right beside Luffy.

shot.fallback: giant warrior with dragon wings facing a shadowy ruler

lines.text: He never needed Luffy's crew to give him a reason. He's had one since chapter 1170.

shot.fallback: giant warrior standing ready for battle

lines.text: So no, Loki isn't the villain Elbaph still thinks he is.
Loki killed his own king, not out of hate, but because somebody finally had to...

shot.fallback: giant prince standing over a fallen king, resolute

self_check.loop: last line loops back into line 1's 'Loki killed his own king' with the reason attached
